samples.summary: `MAX_ROW_PAGE_SPAN` silently clips a legitimately tall table row's content out of pagination and PDF export
samples.evidence: `paginatableRowHeight` returns `Math.min(raw, contentHeight * MAX_ROW_PAGE_SPAN)` (pagination.ts:82). `tl.rowHeights[ri]` is not only the user-dragged minimum — steps 3–4 of `computeTableLayout` derive it from cell content, which is NOT bounded by `normalizeRowHeight` (that only bands the stored user minimum, table-layout.ts:253). A single table row whose cell content genuinely exceeds ~200 pages (~10k lines, e.g. a document whose whole body was pasted into one cell) is now truncated: the split loop stops at the clamp, so the remaining fragments are never emitted on any page and the content vanishes from the canvas and from PDF export. Secondarily, `currentY` then advances by the clamped height while `tl.rowYOffsets` for the following rows were computed from the unclamped one, so the rest of that table is placed at offsets that disagree with the layout table.

samples.summary: The new `lineHeight` band breaks the documented GET→PUT round-trip of the v1 docs content API (write validator accepts what the reader now drops)
samples.evidence: `parseBlockStyleAttrs`'s own doc comment (crdt-attrs.ts:120-129) states the parse drops exactly the values the write-side validator rejects, keeping `GET` → `PUT` identity. The v1 validator only checks finiteness for `BLOCK_STYLE_NUMERIC_FIELDS` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:399-402), so a `PUT` with `style.lineHeight: 100` is accepted and persisted, but the new band at crdt-attrs.ts:148-152 makes the subsequent `GET` (and every renderer) report `DEFAULT_BLOCK_STYLE.lineHeight` instead. A client that reads-modifies-writes therefore silently rewrites the stored spacing. The same asymmetry now exists for `listLevel` (clamped to 8 on read, unvalidated on write), cell `padding` and inline `fontSize`.

samples.summary: A non-finite row height is mapped to 0, which can drop the row from every page instead of placing it
samples.evidence: `paginatableRowHeight` returns 0 for a non-finite raw height (pagination.ts:80). With `rowHeight === 0`, the fits-branch guard `currentY + rowHeight <= contentHeight` (line 136) is false whenever `currentY > contentHeight` — reachable when `contentHeight <= 0`/NaN from a degenerate `pageSetup`, where the fragment loop above can overshoot `currentY`. Control then falls into `while (consumed < rowHeight)` with `rowHeight === 0`, which iterates zero times, so no `PageLine` is emitted for that row at all: the row (and any following-row geometry that depends on it being placed) is missing from the paginated layout rather than merely rendered empty.

samples.summary: `normalizeRowHeights` (plural) is exported but has no callers and is not re-exported from either entry
samples.evidence: A repo-wide grep for `normalizeRowHeights` matches only its own definition at packages/docs/src/model/row-height.ts:42. Neither `src/index.ts` nor `src/node.ts` re-exports it (they export only `MAX_ROW_HEIGHT` / `normalizeRowHeight`), so it is dead code — and knip, which runs on this branch, flags unused exports.
